why: A `where` naming a property no class declares is rejected before the search, under the code `query` gives the same text (contract 0.26.0). The rule is `unknown-class`'s one argument over: a predicate that cannot be asked cannot produce a true negative, and searching anyway would report a typo as a fact about the corpus. `rejected.code` is `undeclared-property` — `query`'s code and not a new one — so a client branching on the codes branches once for both tools. There is no `rejected.step`: `retrieve` has no steps.
